Seminar Title:

Valorization of Cassava (Manihot esculenta L.) Leaves through Sustainable Protein Extraction using Deep Eutectic Solvent and Its Application in Enriching Gluten-Free Bread.

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Food Process Engineering

Speaker Name:

Abhipriya Patra ( Rollno : 521fp1005)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

CH-113

Date and Time:

07 Sep 2026 12.00 Noon

Contact:

Arun Prasath Venugopal

Abstract:

Cassava (Manihot esculenta) leaves represent an underutilized yet valuable source of sustainable plant protein, containing approximately 20&ndash30% protein on a dry-matter basis and a well-balanced amino acid profile. However, the presence of cyanogenic glycosides and condensed tannins limits their nutritional potential. Conventional protein extraction methods, particularly alkaline extraction&ndashisoelectric precipitation (AE-IP), may cause protein denaturation, loss of functional activity, and retention of chemical residues. In this context, the present study investigated the development of a high-quality cassava leaf protein isolate through integrated extraction, green, and process-intensified strategies, followed by its structural and functional modification for food applications. Initially, response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimize the AE-IP method. The optimized conditions yielded a maximum protein content of 21.83 &plusmn 0.41 g/100 g dry matter, extraction yield of 18.31 &plusmn 0.53%, and protein recovery of 69.00 &plusmn 1.31%. The extracted protein exhibited limited in vitro bio accessibility due to the high concentration of cyanide and tannins. However, low-temperature drying (40 &degC for 5 h), followed by repeated washing, effectively reduced cyanide and tannin contents by approximately 89% and 69%, respectively, with a relatively small protein loss (~9.7%). Among the eight DES systems evaluated, DES-8 (lactic acid) exhibited the most favourable extraction performance based on multivariate analysis and principal component analysis. DES-8 extraction produced a protein content of 22.16 &plusmn 0.36 g/100 g dry matter and protein recovery of 73.77 &plusmn 1.05%. The resulting DCPI-D8 exhibited higher total amino acid (91.24%) and essential amino acid (40.36%) contents than the AE-IP-derived protein, while maintaining structural integrity and improved functional properties.

To further enhance extraction efficiency and protein quality, ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent extraction (USDAE) was developed and optimized using RSM. Under the optimized conditions, the process achieved a protein content of 40.56 &plusmn 0.54 g/100 g dry matter, extraction yield of 25.91 &plusmn 0.89%, and recovery yield of 76.72 &plusmn 1.44%. Ultrasound synergistically enhanced cell disruption, mass transfer, and solvent penetration without compromising nutritional quality. The resultant DCPI-UD8 exhibited higher essential amino acid content (43.53%), improved digestibility, reduced antinutritional factors, smaller particle size, porous microstructure, increased &beta-sheet content, and superior thermal stability, indicating its potential for functional food applications. In addition to extraction, DCPI-UD8 was structurally and functionally modified through wet Maillard conjugation with xanthan gum (XG) at different protein ratios. The conjugate prepared at an 8:1 ratio (CPG8:1) exhibited the highest grafting efficiency (35 &plusmn 0.93%). Moderate XG incorporation improved the functional, antioxidant, and rheological properties of the protein, whereas excessive XG caused steric hindrance and aggregation. Rheological and pasting analyses confirmed improved viscoelasticity, thermal stability, and gel stability, highlighting the suitability of CPG8:1 for gluten-free food applications. The application of CPG8:1 in gluten-free sorghum bread demonstrated that 10% incorporation improved dough rheology, crumb structure, texture, and sensory acceptability. The resulting bread exhibited lower hardness and chewiness, improved springiness and cohesiveness, and enhanced crumb and sensory quality. During 6 days of storage, the bread retained moisture and textural stability, indicating the potential of the conjugate to improve the quality and shelf stability of gluten-free bakery products. Overall, this thesis establishes an integrated and sustainable approach for converting detoxified cassava leaves into high-value plant protein through green extraction, ultrasound intensification, and controlled biopolymer conjugation, with promising applications in functional and gluten-free food systems.
